correctness.rationale: On the dual grid, the unnormalized transform of the two-axis support is exactly the additive subspace F=u(chi)+v(psi), by inversion on the factors. Translating a largest entry by a character modulation and scaling it to 1 gives the normalization; the computed minimizer itself has every other entry of modulus strictly below 1. The counting-measure r-power is strictly convex on complex arrays for r>1. Independent permutations fixing the trivial index preserve additivity and the constrained minimum; the unique constrained minimizer therefore has four levels, 1,a,b,t, with t=a+b-1. For M=m-1 and N=n-1 the objective minus 1 is N|a|^r+M|b|^r+MN|t|^r, under a+b-t=1. As a cross-check, weighted Hölder bounds this below by [N^(-1/(r-1))+M^(-1/(r-1))+(MN)^(-1/(r-1))]^(-(r-1))=MN/D^(r-1), with equality at (a,b,t)=(alpha,beta,-1)/D and no other triple. Inverting gives the claimed arm levels by character orthogonality and the center by subtracting the arm masses from 1. At r=2 the result reduces to sqrt((m+n-1)/(mn)), and on equal orders the fixed-r asymptotic follows by retaining the two growing terms in D. The sign is measured on the distinguished sum-normalized representative, not after an arbitrary complex scalar. Its numerator equals mn at r=2, is positive below 2, and for both orders above 2 decreases strictly to 2m+2n-mn. This limit is zero exactly at the finite-r strictly positive boundary (m-2)(n-2)=4; a negative limit gives exactly one crossing after 2. If m=2 the numerator is 2+2 beta>0, and the transpose gives the n=2 case. With equal orders q>=5 solving the crossing equation gives the stated logarithm. Endpoints are not part of the uniqueness assertion.
residual_risks: The script and recorded 4,768 finite evaluations were inspected, not rerun. The assertions covering Fourier arrays use cyclic examples, whereas the proof uses only finite abelian character orthogonality.

value.rationale: A cross is a natural non-product Fourier support beyond the usual transitive synthesis model. The exact result shows how asymmetric arm multiplicities jointly control synthesis at each exponent and gives a concrete cancellation phenomenon: as r passes the unique threshold, the normalized central coefficient can vanish and then become negative even though both punctured axes remain positive. Unlike a single Fourier table, this distinguishes the support of the optimizer and its coefficient signs throughout the parameter range.
residual_risks: The invariant is specific to two unweighted axes; the finite endpoint exponents and more complicated subgroup arrangements are not treated.
